articleTitle: Enhancing Cruise Performance Through PID Controller Tuned with Particle Swarm Optimization Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: The Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller is a widely used feedback control mechanism in various applications, including automobile cruise control systems. The performance of a PID controller is highly dependent on the values of its tuning parameters, which can be challenging to determine in practice. Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) has emerged as a powerful optimization algorithm that can tune the PID controller parameters for optimal performance. The PSO is a metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the social behavior of birds and fish. The PSO-PID is a variant of the PID controller that employs PSO to optimize its tuning parameters. PSO-PID offers several advantages over traditional PID tuning methods, including improved accuracy, stability, and robustness. This paper briefly overviews the PSO-PID algorithm and its application to automobile cruise control systems. The paper discusses the key steps involved in PSO-PID tuning, including initialization, evaluation, update, and termination. It provides an example of how PSO-PID can achieve optimal vehicle speed control. The paper highlights the advantages of PSO-PID over traditional PID tuning methods. PSO-PID is a promising technology for cruise control systems and has the potential to significantly improve the safety, comfort, and efficiency of modern automobiles.

articleTitle: Performance of LQR and PID Controllers for RS-550VC Motor Speed Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Motor speed control is a critical aspect of many industrial and commercial applications. This paper investigates the performance of two widely used control techniques, Linear Quadratic Regulator LQR and Proportional-Integral-Derivative PID, for motor speed control. We perform a simulation study using MATLAB to compare the performance of these two controllers in terms of their ability to track the reference speed profile. The simulation results show that LQR and PID controllers can achieve accurate speed tracking, but their performance characteristics differ significantly. LQR is better in the steady state and overshoot but slower than PID. Our study provides insights into the trade-offs between these two controllers and can guide the selection of an appropriate control technique for a given motor speed control application.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation Research of Wire-Driven Continuum Minimally Invasive Surgical Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of small and variable surgical space segmentation and insufficient dexterity of surgical robots, this paper designs a small and flexible line-driven continuum surgical robot. Firstly, each part of the robot is described; then, the kinematics analysis of the controllable bending bone segment is carried out, and the analysis results are simulated by using MATLAB software, and the operation space pose of different driving line changes of the controllable bending bone segment is obtained; finally, The Monte Carlo method workspace is used for simulation analysis. According to the research results, it is verified that the robot can bend flexibly and supplely, which is suitable for complex small surgery scenarios.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control for Leader-Follower Formation Control of Multiple Mobile Robots Using a Modified C/GMRES Method
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a model predictive control (MPC) approach to address the leader-follower formation control problem of multiple mobile robots. To account for the proprietary dynamics of most commercial mobile robots that can significantly affect the system's control performance, we adopt an acceleration-level pseudo-dynamic control (ALPDC) framework for designing the controller. Furthermore, based on the communication topology of the robots, we design a distributed observer for each follower to estimate the state of the leader. By defining the formation tracking errors of the followers, we formulate the tracking problem as a standard MPC problem. To further enhance the real-time performance of MPC optimization, we propose an improved C/GMRES method based on the fixed-time stability theory. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Research and Analysis of a Computer Vision Based Algorithm for Identifying Ash Deposits in Air Condensing Condensers
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: As one of the important equipment of fossil-fuel power station, air cooler is widely used in the three north regions of China, where coal is rich and water is scarce. Its heat exchange efficiency has a considerable impact on unit efficiency. Therefore, conducting intelligent identification and analysis of ash accumulation in air coolers and effectively cleaning them is of great significance for improving the power generation efficiency of power plants. Considering the color and texture changes caused by the degree of dust accumulation in the visible light image of the surface of the air cooler. A method of identifying and analyzing ash deposition in air cooler based on convolutional neural network transfer learning is proposed. We split the training set, test set, and validation set using 6:2:2. Using a convolutional neural network algorithm model to identify air cooler images with varying degrees of fouling, and mining and analyzing the corresponding relationship between air cooler fouling images and fin cleaning. The results show that for the existing 5 levels of air coolers with ash accumulation, the model with higher recognition rate is Vgg19, with recognition accuracy of 0.98 and recall rate of 0.98, respectively, while the model with lower recognition accuracy is AlexNet, with an accuracy rate of 0.78. The proposed method for analyzing the ash accumulation status of air coolers can directly, real-time, and quantitatively analyze the on-site ash accumulation of air coolers, and provide reference and new considerations for achieving intelligent cleaning and operation and maintenance on site.

articleTitle: An Iterative Method to Control Angle of Attack and Sideslip Angle Based on Model Correction
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Aiming at controllingthe angle of attack and sideslip angle for air breathing aircraft at ignition time of the engine after separation quickly and accurately. This paper proposes an iterative method to control the angle of attack and sideslip angle based on model correction. Firstly, the relationship between those angles and overload which measured by IMU system is established, so the angle of attack and sideslip angle are predicted by using trim aerodynamic model. At the same time, aiming at reducing the deviation between the actual force of the aircraft and the force calculated by the trim aerodynamic model, a multi-dimensional Newton iteration is used to correct the prediction method by real time. Validated by simulation, the deviation of the angle of attack at the ignition time of the engine is less than 0.3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\circ$</tex> and the deviation of sideslip angle is less than 0. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4^{\circ}$</tex> by using the method proposed in this paper. This method has high engineering application value.

articleTitle: Design and Strategy Research of UAV Dynamic Take-Off and Landing Platform Based on Inertial Stability Control Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: In this paper, a dynamic takeoff and landing device of UAV based on inertial stability control platform is designed. The platform can effectively isolate the disturbance caused by the disturbance of carrier (vehicle, ship, etc.), and provide a stable platform for the takeoff and landing of UAV. During the take-off stage of UAV, the azimuth pointing Angle of the apron can be calculated in real time according to the first target point of UAV mission route, and the attitude adjustment mechanism can drive the UAV to ensure that the nose points to the first target point of UAV mission route in real time. In the landing stage of the UAV, the orientation Angle of the apron can be calculated in real time according to the nose orientation, so as to ensure that the orientation of the apron is consistent with the nose of the UAV during the moving process of the carrier. There is no need to adjust the nose in real time according to the rotation Angle of the carrier during the moving landing of the UAV. This method greatly reduces the difficulty of the moving landing of the UAV and saves about 10% of the electric power of the UAV. After landing on the platform, the UAV can realize automatic centering, locking, charging and other fully autonomous processes without human intervention.

articleTitle: Modeling and Implicit Inversion of Butterfly Hysteresis in Dielectric Elastomer Actuated System
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Butterfly hysteresis nonlinearity is a unique type of hysteresis characteristic that is distinct from the traditional single-loop hysteresis characteristic, demonstrating non-monotonic and multi-peak features between input and output. In this paper, we analyze the causes of butterfly hysteresis non-linearity in dielectric elastomer actuated systems and propose a butterfly hysteresis model based on the classical relay operator. To compensate for the butterfly non-monotonic hysteresis nonlinearity in the dielectric elastomer actuated systems, an novel implicit inverse compensation algorithm is proposed. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the established model and the inverse compensation algorithm.

articleTitle: A Method of Magnetometer Relative Reference Calibration for Micro-Nano Satellite and Its Application in Orbit
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: For a low-cost micro-nano satellite that uses magnetometer as the core sensor of attitude determination system, a calibration method of relative reference between multiple magnetometer is proposed. The influence of satellite magnetic environment on magnetic field intensity measurement is studied. After considering remanence, induction and installation deviation, an accurate measurement model of magnetometer is proposed. Without introducing other high-performance attitude sensors, the relative relationship between the measurement data of different magnetometer is derived, and a magnetometer relative reference calibration method based on the least square method is proposed. Mathematical simulation shows that the proposed method reduces the relative measurement error of the magnetometer from 2000 nT to 50 nT, and then uses the telemetry data of the satellite in orbit to calibrate several magnetometer of the satellite. After injecting new parameters, the attitude difference of satellites with different magnetometer as the reference decreases from 16 degrees to less than 2 degrees, indicating that the consistency of the magnetometer reference has been significantly improved, which verifies the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Output Feedback Tracking Control for Quantized Input/Output Nonlinear Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: This paper focuses on the adaptive output feedback tracking control of uncertain nonlinear systems with both quantized input and output. The only available signal is the non-differentiable quantized output, which makes the adaptive quantized controller hard to achieve via output feedback. Our research shows that this difficulty can be circumvented by utilizing the well known dynamic surface control (DSC) technique and introducing extra continuous virtual control signals for stability analysis only. Furthermore, it is proved that all the closed-loop system signals are bounded, and the tracking error can converge to a small residual set by adjusting some design parameters appropriately. Simulation results are given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Spray Cooling Control Based on Model Predictive Control: Status, Challenges and Prospects
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: The continuous development of modern industry has led to the widespread use of high-temperature equipment, making efficient cooling equipment vital for industrial development. However, the complexity of the spray cooling model makes traditional control methods inadequate for achieving precise control. In contrast, the model predictive control method can address this problem effectively, thereby possessing significant application value in the study of spray cooling. This paper introduces the basic principles and mathematical model of spray cooling, discusses the limitations of the traditional MPC-based spray cooling control strategy, and presents four improved MPC methods. Additionally, this paper highlights the challenges associated with spray cooling control based on model predictive control and provides a perspective on the future development direction of spray cooling control based on model predictive control.

articleTitle: Design and Motion Analysis of an Underactuated Finger Based on the Coupled and Self-Adaptive Linkage Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Underactuated prosthetic hands possess excellent adaptability, yet they often suffer from issues such as complex structure, limited anthropomorphism, and reduced stability. To address these concerns, this paper presents a novel finger with coupled-adaptive functionality, consisting of three joints and two degrees of freedom (DOFs). It exhibits notable anthropomorphism, heightened stability, strong adaptability, and a simplified structure. This finger utilizes a novel coupled-adaptive linkage mechanism, enabling coupled motion in free space and self-adaptive motion while grasping diverse objects. Additionally, a series of simulation analyses have provided evidence that the finger can effectively and stably perform coupled movements and adaptively grasp objects of different shapes and sizes.

articleTitle: Prediction of NOx Emission Concentration Based on Weighted Optimal Combination Model
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: In order to achieve accurate prediction of NOx emissions concentration from coal-fired boiler outlets, this paper proposes a nitrogen oxide emission concentration prediction model based on a weighted optimization combination model. Firstly, in order to extract the depth time-frequency information in the data, the RLMD decomposition is used to decompose the input data. Secondly, considering the existence of redundant information in the input data, the ReliefF feature selection is used to select the strongly correlated feature variables as the modeling input. Finally, in order to improve the accuracy of the prediction model, Extreme Learning Machine (ELM), Echo State Network (ESN), Deep Neural Networks (DNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) are combined, and the weights of the four models are optimized using the ant colony algorithm to construct the NOx emission concentration prediction model. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm has a prediction error of less than 2% for NOx emission concentration under different operating conditions, and can achieve accurate prediction of NOx emission concentration from coal-fired boiler outlets.

articleTitle: Calculation of Carbon Emissions and Analysis of Influencing Factors in Thermal Power Industry in Jilin Province
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: In this paper, the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission of thermal power industry in Jilin Province is taken as the research object, and the carbon emission measurement model of thermal power industry is constructed. This paper calculates the energy consumption and carbon emissions of the thermal power industry in Jilin Province in the past six years from 2016–2021. This paper analyzes the carbon emission law of the thermal power industry in Jilin Province, and discusses the factors affecting the carbon emission of the thermal power industry in Jilin Province.

articleTitle: Adaptive Hybrid Neural Network Sliding Mode Control of Ultrasonic Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Nonlinear disturbances such as viscous friction, static friction and external disturbances exist in ultrasonic motors, which seriously affect their high-performance motion control process. To realize the high precision scanning motion of ultrasonic motor, an adaptive hybrid neural network sliding mode control (AHNN-SMC) method is designed. The neural network basis function part adopts a combination of Gaussian basis and partial friction model, combined with an adaptive algorithm to achieve online nonlinear compensation of the ultrasonic motor. In order to solve the problem of overestimation of switching control gain caused by the difficulty of accurate estimation of uncertain upper bound in the control process, adaptive switching gain is further adopted in this paper to cut down the influence of chatter in the control process. In order to verify the performance of AHNN-SMC in ultrasonic motor scanning motion control, position tracking simulation experiments are performed for sinusoidal signals with a maximum displacement of 20mm and compared with several algorithms. The results show that the maximum tracking error (MAE) of AHNN-SMC is 3.15 μ m and the mean error (RMSE) is 1.25 μ m, and the results indicate that the method has good position tracking performance.

articleTitle: Analysis and Optimization of Wind Turbine Yaw Regulation Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: With the rapid development of wind power generation, wind turbines will develop with the goal of more stable, safer and higher power generation. However, the traditional yaw control system needs to follow the wind direction and need to be adjusted at any time, although the wind turbine's wind accuracy has been improved, but this will also make the wind turbine make a useless yaw and increase the load of the wind turbine, which will not only reduce the output power of the turbine, but also reduce the service life of the turbine. Therefore, a wind turbine yaw strategy based on the wind direction prediction results is proposed, and a new yaw strategy is proposed by combining the wind direction prediction results with the actual needs of the site, and compared with the traditional yaw strategy, the new wind turbine yaw strategy is proposed to have better results.

articleTitle: Adaptive Inverse Compensation Output Feedback Control for Dielectric Elastomer Actuator Motion Control System
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive inverse compensation output feedback control scheme is designed for the dielectric elastomer actuator (DEA) motion control system. First, the controller adopts the radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) approximator, which avoids the parameter identification of DEA motion control system. Second, a long short term memory neural network-based hysteresis inverse model (LSTMNN-BIM) is trained to compensate the hysteresis nonlinearity. Third, by designing a high-gain state observer to estimate the unknown state variables of the system, only the output of the system needs to be measured. Stability analysis shows that all signals in system are eventually uniformly bounded. Finally, simulation experiment is conducted, and the experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Dynamic Analysis of Mechanical Controlled Two Degree-of-Freedom QZS Vibration Isolators
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: A basic one degree-of-freedom (1DOF) quasi-zero stiffness (QZS) vibration isolator is composed of two lateral springs used as negative stiffness mechanism and one vertical spring used as positive stiffness mechanism. Three types of two degree of freedom (2DOF) isolators are composed of the 1DOF isolators in series, namely grounded-grounded model (GGM), bottom-springs grounded model (BGM) and top-springs grounded model (TGM). In this paper, these three models are improved with a method of mechanical control and the displacement transmissibility equations of them are derived. Then, the simulation comparison is made. The results show that the performance of the three mechanical controlled models is significantly better than that of the former.

articleTitle: A 5G-Based Switching Method Between a Local Controller and an Edge Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: With the rapid development of edge computing, industrial automation has evolved a two-layer distributed computing architecture, including local controllers communicating through wired networks and edge controllers communicating wirelessly. The edge controllers in existing studies use WIFI, which has a limited working distance and requires independent network deployment, so they are unsuitable for future large-scale complex industrial production. At present, 5G technology is undergoing rapid development in the field of industrial automation, with wide coverage and excellent mobility, gradually becoming suitable for future large-scale and complex industrial production scenarios. Therefore, this paper proposed an SW5G method based on 5G, which combined the local controller with the edge controller. The controllers were switched according to the constantly changing 5G network transmission delay, thereby optimizing the overall system control performance. Finally, simulation experiments demonstrated good control performance of SW5G in various network scenarios.

articleTitle: Research on Vehicle and Pedestrian Detection Algorithm in Foggy Weather Based on Improved YOLOv5s
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of the bad performance of current automatic driving perception algorithm in foggy weather, this paper proposes a vehicle and pedestrian detection algorithm in foggy weather based on improved YOLOv5s. Firstly, based on Cityscapes dataset, artificially generate foggy images of three concentrations to form Foggy Cityscapes dataset. Secondly, C3STR structure is introduced into the backbone network to better improve the extraction ability of model for global features. Thirdly, de-weighted BiFPN is introduced into the neck network, adding a jump connection from backbone directly to PAN, strengthening the feature fusion and reducing the loss of feature information. Finally, EIoU is used in the boundary box loss function, which improves the regression precision and accelerates the convergence speed. The experiment results show that the algorithm proposed in this paper achieves good results in both synthetic foggy image dataset and real foggy image dataset, and meets the real-time requirement, which has certain practicability.

articleTitle: Fault Detection for Positive Switched Systems with All Modes Unstable
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Exponential stability, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{1}$</tex> -gain performance and fault detection are investigated in this paper for continuous positive switched system (PSS) when there exists no stable subsystems. To eliminate the instability brought by the unstable modes ensure the exponential stbility, a time-driven switching strategy is proposed by means of the average dwell time approach. Then, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{1}$</tex> -gain performance for the PSS is guaranteed. Additionally, the stable filter design is converted into the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{1}$</tex> -gain analysis. Sufficient conditions are deduced to guarantee the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{1}$</tex> -gain performance with exponential stability in terms of linear matrices inequalities (LMIs). Finally, an example is provided to test and verify the effectiveness and practicality.

articleTitle: Segmented Prediction Model of Lithium-ion Battery Remaining Useful Life Based on LSTM and SVR
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: As an important part of battery health management, accurate prediction on remaining useful life of lithium-ion battery can maintain and replace the batteries in advance to guarantee the safety and stability of the energy storage system. Most extant models use a single model throughout the entire stage for prediction, which may lead to the decrease of the accuracy for subsequent prediction due to insufficient learning, as well as disability to predict battery remaining useful life with data from other batteries. To solve these issues, a segmented prediction model of lithium-ion battery remaining useful life is proposed. In this method, the knee point of the capacity decline curve is detected and then long short-term memory and support vector regression models are used to predict the remaining useful life before and after the knee point, respectively. The experimental prediction results represent that the proposed method achieves higher prediction accuracy compared with long short-term memory method.

articleTitle: S-Shape Soft Robot Based on PVDF/Copper Bilayer Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: At present, many soft robots suffer from poor motion performance and limited environmental adaptability. To address this challenge, innovative structural designs have been proposed. In this paper, we introduce a novel soft piezoelectric microrobot with a S-shape structure. Our work achieves two significant accomplishments: (1) With a weight of only 0.058g and a length of 1cm, the robot uses resonance to achieve motion and exhibits excellent motion performance, capable of reaching a speed of 41.2 BL/s. (2) The symmetrical body structure and vibration modes of the robot enable it to maintain high-speed motion (16 BL/s) even after flipping over, demonstrating its enhanced environmental adaptability. Overall, our new structural design opens up new opportunities for microrobots to improve their motion performance and environmental adaptability.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation for a Novel Semi-Active Seat-suspension with a Cam-Roller-Spring Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Semi-active suspension has less energy consumption and low cost compared with active suspension, so it is more widely used. In this paper, a novel semi-active seat-suspension with cam-roller-spring mechanism (CRSM) is presented and the human body is considered. A simple nonlinear control strategy is proposed, that is, the variable damping coefficient is designed to be proportional to the square of the relative motion speed between the sprung mass and the tire. To verify the effect of the novel seat-suspension and control strategy, a method of 3D visual modeling and simulation in MATLAB/SimMechanics is proposed and the model is established and simulated under the excitation of the bump road. The results show that the seat-suspension and control strategy can greatly improve the stability speed, which is nearly 90% higher than the passive seat-suspension. The results also show that the cam-roller-spring mechanism can obviously enhance the attenuation effect of the seat-suspension on the road excitation.

articleTitle: Phenomenological Modeling and End-Point Trajectory Tracking Control of a Flexible Beam with Pneumatic Soft Actuators
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: As the basic construction of flexible mechanical systems, the flexible beam and its control problem have attracted widespread attention in recent years. This paper takes a flexible beam with pneumatic soft actuators (FBPSA) as the research object and studies its phenomenological modeling and end-point trajectory tracking control strategy. Firstly, we develop an experimental platform for the FBPSA and perform tests on it, gathering its input and output data. Using these collected data, we analyzed the motion characteristics of the FBPSA. Subsequently, a phenomenological model is established to describe the motion characteristics of the system, and the parameters of this model are identified through a large amount of the collected experimental data. Then, a combined feedforward-feedback control strategy is proposed to achieve the end-point trajectory tracking control of the system. Finally, three sets of experiments are carried out to verify the accuracy of the established model and the effectiveness and superiority of the control strategy.

articleTitle: Improved Mode-Free Adaptive Control for Piezoelectric Micro-Positioning Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Piezoelectric micro-positioning (PMP) platforms have been widely applied due to their fast response and high resolution. However, the strong nonlinearities in the PMP plat-form seriously degrade the positioning accuracy. In this study, an improved model-free adaptive control (MFAC) method is proposed to solve the nonlinearities in the PMP platform. In the improved MFAC, the classical dynamic linearization (DL) is extended to a neural network (NN)-based DL. That is, the unmodeled dynamics in the DL is approximated by aNN. Based on the NN-based DL, the performance of the improved MFAC is better than the traditional MFAC. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, experiments are conducted on the PMP platform. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve the satisfactory control performance.

articleTitle: IIoT Network Intrusion Detection Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems are subject to intrusion attacks that may cause devastating damage. However, common security mechanisms may not be applicable as IIoT systems and standard IT networks are fundamentally different. Therefore, it is necessary to consider different security factors and performance metrics when addressing the vulnerabilities and security demands of IIoT. Machine Learning (ML) has proven to be an effective tool in the development of security mechanisms and Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) for IIoT. This paper presents the implementation of multiple IDS models using six ML algorithms. These models were evaluated on the WUSTL-IIoT-2021 dataset, and their performance was analyzed and compared. Among the six models, the model constructed using the Random Forest (RF) algorithm achieved an accuracy of 99.97%, which is significantly higher than the accuracy achieved by previously reported models in the literature. The results demonstrate the significance of this work and highlight the potential of ML-based IDS models in ensuring the security and safety of IIoT systems.

articleTitle: A Multi-Domain Feature Fusion Method for NOx Concentration Prediction in SCR Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) systems exhibit characteristics such as nonlinearity and significant hysteresis. In order to establish an accurate predictive model for the outlet NOx emission concentration in SCR, a modeling algorithm based on multi-domain feature fusion is proposed. Firstly, the original data is processed using the boxplot method to remove outliers, and the K-nearest neighbors (KNN) algorithm is employed to impute the removed outlier points based on sample distance. The delay time of each variable is estimated using the maximal information coefficient (MI), and the data is reconstructed accordingly. Then, deep features are extracted using singular spectrum analysis, and the final input variables for the model are determined using an adaptive composite feature selection algorithm. Finally, a predictive model for the outlet nitrogen oxide concentration in the SCR system is constructed. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves an average absolute percentage error (MAPE) of less than 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, thus accurately predicting the outlet nitrogen oxide concentration in the SCR system.

articleTitle: Dynamic Sensing Modeling of Dielectric Elastomer Sensors Based on GRU Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Dielectric elastomer sensor (DES) is a flexible sensor that can perform free bending deformation, thus it has broad application prospects in the fields of medical electronics, wearable devices, soft robots, etc. Previous studies have mostly focused on exploring the static sensing characteristics of the DES. Considering that the DES may be used in dynamic conditions, it is very meaningful to study its dynamic sensing characteristics to broaden its application ranges. In this paper, a dynamic sensing model of the DES is established based on the gate recurrent unit (GRU) neural network. Firstly, the structure of the DES and the construction of the experimental system are introduced. In addition, the dynamic sensing characteristics of the DES are analyzed by conducting several sets of experiments, which shows that the DES has significant rate-dependent hysteresis nonlinearities, multivalued mapping and memory characteristics. After that, the dynamic sensing model of the DES is built based on the GRU neural network to describe the above dynamic sensing characteristics. Next, the dynamic displacement and force sensing models of the DES are trained according to the dynamic displacement-capacitance and dynamic force-capacitance experimental data, respectively. Finally, several experiments are performed to verify the effectiveness and generalization ability of the established dynamic sensing model.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network-based Identification of Communication Room Indicator Status in Complex Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Recognizing and detecting the status indicators of communication room equipment is crucial to improving the security and stability of communication networks. Deep learning-based recognition methods have demonstrated higher accuracy and real-time performance for image recognition, with YOLOv5s being a small network-scale model that achieves high precision and real-time performance. It is particularly suitable for detecting indicator lights in computer room environments. However, target recognition faces significant challenges and limitations in complex production environments, such as physical phenomena like light reflection and refraction, which can make feature extraction and fusion difficult. In this paper, we address these challenges by enhancing the YOLOv5s network with a SimAM attention mechanism module. This improves the network's attention to critical information and enhances its feature fusion capability. Our goal is to improve the accuracy and recognition precision of the model in complex communication room environments. We conducted experiments on a self-built dataset based on the actual production environment in the server room. The results show that the improved YOLOv5s network achieved 94.7% recognition accuracy and 95.0% mAP-50, which is 1.6 and 1.3 percentage points higher than the baseline network YOLOv5s, respectively. The improved model showed better performance in the actual production environment of the complex communication server room.

articleTitle: Skill-Dependent Representations for Object Navigation
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Object navigation tasks aim to guide an agent to reach a target object with a monocular visual RGB sensor. The agent is required to possess various abilities, such as exploring unknown areas for environmental learning and navigating to the discovered target, to accomplish the tasks. However, most existing methods implicitly establish a holistic representation of these abilities, lacking interpretability and increasing training difficulty. In skill-based approaches, different skills are often fed with the same features, necessitating further learning of more suitable features for each skill by the agent. Therefore, we propose a Skill-Dependent Representations navigation frAMe-work (SDRAM), including a skill selection strategy, and two skill modules: exploration and navigation. The exploration skill utilizes high-level object representations and target embedding, while the navigation strategy employs detailed visual representations that are widely used in the state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. Our method outperforms the SOTA models in the AI2Thor environment with higher navigation success rate, and we demonstrate that our framework has good generalizability.

articleTitle: An SoS Architecture and Intelligent Airfield Isomer Robot for WIG Effect Aircraft Carrier Based on Cloud Sea Computing in 5G OGCE
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Based on the fifth and/or sixth generation of mobile communication(5G/6G), and cloud sea computing (CSC) in 5G open grid computing environment (OGCE), a model of wing-in-ground (WIG) effect aircraft carrier (EAC) based on model of manta ray and an intelligent airfield isomer robot (IAIR) are presented by this paper. The structure of the WIG EAC consists of a multi-hull ship model and a center-body of a blended wing body (BWB) configuration of commercial aircraft framework, which is based on the reconfiguring tube-and-(sweptback) wing (TAW) (e.g., Airbus A380, Boeing 777X), the combinatorial structure of a center-body can be configured by intersecting and overlapping framework variant (IOFV) of two aircraft (2A) (IOFV-2A) with the TAW configuration, or, IOFV of three aircraft (IOFV-3A) with the TAW configuration. This IAIR is composed of a takeoff-landing (runway) working deck platform (TOLWDP, or WDP) robot and a three-overlapping Venus flytrap Nelumbo lutea (hand type) robot (TO-VFNL-R), a telescopic positioning grip hand (grab-hook) type robot (TPGHTR), and its other robots. A TOLWDP (WDP) robot can bear the weight of the heaviest fighter jet, which is able to take off and land on the WIG EAC, such as Shenyang J-15, J-16D, J-35, and Sukhoi Su-35, Su-57, and also can take off and land and catapult the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). This WIG EAC has a large hangar that used for sea rescue and support, and when supported by carrier-based aircraft and underwater robots, can intercept the aircraft carrier fleets and submarine fleets and unmanned submarine. Under the support of the CSC in 5G OGCE, the aircraft can safely be berthed and docked and land on the TOLWDP under the command and control (C2) of the distributed control cloud, to realize the various tasks of air-sea WIG EAC based on CSC in 5G OGCE.

Author Keywords: three-overlapping Venus flytrap - Nelumbo Lutea hand type robot
blended wing body configuration of commercial aircraft

articleTitle: Randomness-Enhanced Grey Wolf Optimizer for Inverse Kinematics Solution of Redundant Robotic Manipulators
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: In this study, a randomness-enhanced grey wolf optimizer (REGWO) is proposed to efficiently solve the inverse kinematics (IK) of redundant manipulators. REGWO is an improved version of the grey wolf optimizer (GWO), and it overcomes its shortcomings concerning premature convergence and low population diversity. In the REGWO, more random individuals are introduced to affect population updates, which is beneficial for the global search of the algorithm. A fitness function composed of position and orientation errors is proposed to solve the optimization problem. An eight-degree-of-freedom serial manipulator was applied to verify the superiority of the REGWO. The results were compared with the classical GWO and other four state-of-the-art algorithm results. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed REGWO can quickly and accurately solve the IK problem of a redundant manipulator.

articleTitle: Anti-Disturbance Control for PEMFC Air Supply Systems with Input Quantization
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Anti-disturbance control of the proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) air supply subsystem in face of disturbances and uncertainties is of essence in guaranteeing the system performance and safety. This paper is concentrated on the precise control of a crucial performance indicator, the oxygen excess ratio (OER). Firstly, a hysteretic quantizer is introduced to reduce the communication burden in controller channels. Then, an active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) strategy is introduced by constructing an extended state observer (ESO) to estimate and eliminate the coupled disturbance including rapid load variations, parametric uncertainties and quantization errors. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified compared with the traditional PID control method by a simulation test.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Object Detection Based on Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Few-shot object detection is a challenging research topic in the field of computer vision. In scenarios with a limited number of training samples, traditional object detection algorithms often suffer from overfitting, leading to subpar classification accuracy and imprecise localization. To address these challenges, we propose a few-shot object detection algorithm based on contrastive learning, encompassing the design of data strategies and model structures. To mitigate the issues arising from limited data and insufficient intra-class diversity, we introduce data augmentation strategies involving saliency-mixed image enhancement and data resampling. Additionally, to tackle problems such as misclassification of new instances and inaccurate object localization, we design a comprehensive model structure for few-shot object detection based on contrastive learning. Experimental evaluations are conducted on general datasets PASCAL VOC. The results demonstrate the high effectiveness and practicality of the proposed approach in few-shot object detection tasks, underscoring its significant research significance and practical application value.

articleTitle: Design and Experimental Study of Air Cooler Magnetic Adsorption Intelligent Cleaning Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: The air-cooled unit works in a low humidity environment and the air contains a lot of dust, which is easily adsorbed on the surface of the fins, leading to a reduction in the heat transfer performance of the finned tubes and affecting the efficiency of the unit, so it needs to be cleaned regularly. In this paper, we developed a magnetic adsorption intelligent cleaning robot for the air cooler wall surface. Firstly, the design of each module of the robot is completed according to the environment of the air cooler wall; secondly, COMSOL software is used to simulate the permanent magnets of different sizes and magnetic circuits to complete the magnetic circuit design of the adsorption mechanism and the adjustment of each parameter, and through the simulation and comparison analysis of the four basic magnetic circuits, it is concluded that the maximum permanent magnet utilization rate of type B magnetic circuit is 57.265%, and when the size parameter of the permanent magnet is When the size of permanent magnet is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{150}\mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{50}\mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{10}\mathbf{mm}$</tex> and the size of iron yoke is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{430}\mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{200}\mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{2}\mathbf{mm}$</tex>, the volume ratio of adsorption force is the largest; finally, the robot's overrunning performance, loading capacity and running speed are tested. The robot can cross a cylindrical obstacle with a diameter of 10mm when going down and a cylindrical obstacle with a diameter of 6mm when going up; the maximum load can reach 16Kg; the maximum moving speed reaches 5.67m/min. The robot can complete the test well and meet the corresponding The robot can complete the test well and meet the corresponding performance requirements, and the experiment verifies the reasonableness of the robot structure design.

articleTitle: Adaptive Neural Backstepping Approximated Inverse Control for a Class of Fractional-Order Hysteretic Nonlinear Time-Delay Systems with Unknown Control Direction
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: The wide application of motion control system based on intelligent material actuator in soft robot, this paper proposes a neural adaptive fractional-order backstepping approximated inverse control (NAFBAIC) strategy for a class of fractional-order time-delay systems with unknown control direction, and hysteretic nonlinearities as input. The main innovations are as follows: 1)Without establishing an exact inverse model of hysteresis, efficient control is achieved for the first time in a fractional-order system; 2)By applying the frequency distribution model, the finite fractional-order state-space representation is transformed into infinite dimension, and the Lyapunov functions is constructed on the basis; 3)The Nussbaum function is introduced into the fractional-order system to solve the problem of unknown control direction; 4)The finite covering lemma is combined with the neural network to approximate the unknown nonlinear function with time-delay in the systems, which reduces the tracking error and improves the control accuracy. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Breast Cancer Prediction Using Classical Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Machine Learning is an emerging topic of study nowadays. Due to their extensive capacity for data exploration and the discovery of illuminating patterns, machine learning, and data mining techniques have become extremely popular. Data mining techniques are also used in the healthcare industry and have proven particularly effective for cancer prognosis and prediction. Breast cancer is the second most significant factor in women's cancer-related death rates. In that situation, early detection of benign and malignant stages of breast cancer can enable the patient, and the doctor administers the appropriate treatments. In this study, a breast cancer dataset of 569 instances and 32 features were chosen to predict the stages of breast cancer. Four classification algorithms are employed: Support Vector Machine, K Nearest Neighbor, Multi layer Perceptron, and Radial Basis Neural Network. The algorithm's performance regarding Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and Roc Area are compared, and it is found that SVM outperformed the others with an accuracy rate of 98.05%. The paper also demonstrated how feature selection strategies might shorten training times before proposing a reliable and universal model for predicting the breast cancer stage.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Localisation and Mapping with Fiducial Markers Based on Extended Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Localisation ability is a prerequisite for the realisation of autonomous systems. In this paper, the extended Kalman filter is used to fuse the encoder information with the information of the camera fiducial markers detection and realise the SLAM algorithm. A new observation model is used considering both the position and orientation of the fiducial markers. The algorithm is implemented using robot operating system and tested in simulation and real environments. The test results show that the algorithm can achieve the expected result, and prove that multi-information fusion has a better effect than single-sensor positioning.

articleTitle: Parallel Vision/Force Interactive Control of Parallel Robots with Uncertainty Compensation
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: This paper develops a novel force control method-ology: parallel vision/force interactive control, and applies it to the control of parallel robots. This control methodology is an advanced vision-based computed torque control that directly controls position and force in the image feature space. The creativity of this approach is the pose estimation of a parallel robot with visual information and coupling force feedback and vision information in parallel. A Gough-Stewart platform is taken into account to validate this approach.
